subject: Discovery Recap: Private/VPC requirements for FinHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finhealth.com>, Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@finhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap: Private/VPC requirements for FinHealth

Hi Alex / Sarah,

Thanks again for a productive conversation this morning — appreciate the time. Per our call, I wanted to recap the main pain points, success criteria, and next steps so we have alignment on what a Private/VPC engagement would need to cover.

Pain points / drivers:
- Regulated data (PHI) handling: strict isolation and auditability requirements from compliance and legal teams.
- Key management: must support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and key rotation policies.
- Network constraints: restricted egress, allow-listing outbound paths, and the option for air-gapped deployment for sensitive workloads.
- Operational visibility: detailed audit logs and per-request metadata for forensic and billing purposes.
- Model governance: need to control which models are served (BYOM consideration) and ensure reproducible model versions for audits.

Current stack (as discussed):
- Primary apps hosted in FinHealth VPC on AWS (us-east-1), internal model evaluation infra currently on-prem.
- Identity: Okta SSO for engineers + SCIM provisioning.
- Networking: existing VPN + dedicated Direct Connect to cloud; on-prem systems sometimes isolated for production PHI flows.

Success criteria for a pilot / POC:
- Deployment in a Private/VPC configuration with customer-managed KMS integration.
- Network egress controls and allow-listing validated by FinHealth networking team.
- Latency target: p95 inference < 200ms for typical 512-token requests on target endpoints (we can iterate on sizing).
- Auditability: request/response logging with retention policy and access controls that meet FinHealth security requirements.
- Hand-off to security for a deep-dive and evidence package (SOC2, pen test summaries, architecture diagrams).

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
1) I attached a Redwood Private/VPC checklist and a sample network diagram we discussed — please confirm any missing items (Attachment: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf, finhealth-network-diagram.png). (owner: Marissa)
2) FinHealth security to share required network egress rules and CI/CD access patterns so we can validate firewall rules. (owner: Alex / Sarah)
3) Schedule a security deep-dive with Rishi (infrastructure & SRE lead) to walk through KMS/HSM, audit logs, and deployment topology — proposed: next Tue/Wed. (owner: Rishi)
4) Internal: prepare SOC2 artifact list & drafting of prelim integration SOW for pricing estimates. (owner: Marissa / Vivek)

Open questions we flagged on the call:
- Do you need an air-gapped, physically isolated on-prem option for production, or would a VPC-only private deployment meet compliance?
- Are there any specific cipher suites / HSM vendors you must use for KMS?
- Expected throughput (RPS) and concurrency for pilot traffic so we can size GPU pools.

I’ll follow up with calendar invites for the security deep-dive and share the checklist link in HubSpot. If anything above needs correction, call it out and I’ll update.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting the security team synced.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0148

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, IT Security <security@finhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Private/VPC requirements for FinHealth

Thanks Marissa — this summary is great and matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications from the security team: 

1) For the air-gap question: at minimum we need the capability to run the model-serving surface within our VPC with no internet egress for PHI endpoints. An air-gapped physical on-prem option is preferred for a subset of very sensitive workflows, but wed like to validate VPC-only first.

2) HSM vendor: we currently use AWS CloudHSM for key storage, but we can accept integrations with third-party HSMs if required.

3) Throughput: pilot scope would be ~50 concurrent requests (p50 latency target ~75ms), scaling to 300 concurrent in production.

A few asks: 
- Can you confirm whether Redwood supports Okta SCIM provisioning for service accounts and if SAML SSO will integrate with your console?
- Also, will we be able to bring our own models (we’re evaluating a couple of fine-tuned variants) or do you require using curated models from Redwood's catalog for Private deployments?
- Finally, rough cost guidance for a 3-month pilot (GPU reservations + private deployment overhead) would help our procurement team.

I’ve looped in our security mailbox for visibility. We can set the deep-dive for Tue 24th if that works for Rishi.

Alex
VP, Engineering — FinHealth
alex.turner@finhealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finhealth.com>, Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@finhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Private/VPC requirements for FinHealth

Alex — perfect, thanks for the detail and the throughput numbers. Quick answers below and proposed next steps.

Answers:
- Okta / SSO: Redwood Private supports SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning for service accounts and user groups; we’ll share a short integration checklist for Okta.
- BYOM (bring-your-own-model): Yes — our Private offering supports customer-owned models. We allow pinned versions and reproduceable rollout policies; we’ll note any model-format constraints in the checklist.
- Cost guidance: I’ll attach a back-of-envelope estimate for a 3-month pilot (included in the checklist). Full pricing will be part of the SOW but expect GPU reservation + private deployment premium; Vivek will work with procurement on final numbers.

Proposed next steps / calendar items:
1) Security deep-dive: Tue, Mar 24, 10:00am ET — Rishi will lead and bring KMS/HSM and audit log owners. (Invite sent)
2) Share integration artifacts: I uploaded the checklist + network diagram to HubSpot and linked the DocuSign placeholder for the SOW. (Links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890, https://www.docusign.com/finhealth/agreements/ABCD1234)
3) Procurement intro: Vivek will pick up pricing and draft a preliminary SOW for review by Mar 30.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf, finhealth-network-diagram.png

If useful, we can also run a small benchmark with one of your fine-tuned models in a staging Private deployment to validate latency/RPS before a full pilot. Let me know and we’ll coordinate resources.

Thanks — looking forward to next week’s deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0148
